title: Week 2 Quiz: Correlative Conjunctions and Conjunctive Adverbs
summary: 20 questions · 20 minutes. Do it alone, without notes, then upload a screenshot of your score to Google Classroom.

blocks.title: Before you start
items: Do the quiz alone, without your notes.
You have 20 minutes. The timer starts when you press Start.
At the end, take a screenshot of your score and upload it to the quiz assignment on Google Classroom.

blocks.title: Week 2 Quiz: Correlative Conjunctions and Conjunctive Adverbs

questions.q: ___ the doctor and the nurse were kind.
You can ___ text me or call me.
___ the TV nor the radio was working.
She speaks not only Arabic ___ French.
Neither my parents nor my brother ___ about the party.
Either the teacher or the students ___ wrong.
Which is correct?
c: He likes neither tea nor coffee.
He likes neither tea or coffee.
He neither likes tea nor coffee likes.
He doesn't like neither tea nor coffee.

questions.q: Which is balanced?
c: She is both clever and she is hard-working.
She is both clever and works hard.
She is both clever and hard-working.
She both is clever and hard-working.

questions.q: Which is correct?
c: Not only did he lost his keys, but he also lost his phone.
Not only he did lose his keys but he also lost his phone.
Not only he lost his keys, but also his phone.
Not only did he lose his keys, but he also lost his phone.

questions.q: The road was closed; ___, we were late.
He was injured; ___, he finished the race.
Fruit is healthy. ___, it is cheap.
Take a map; ___, you might get lost.
Which is punctuated correctly?
c: It was late; therefore, we left.
It was late, therefore we left.
It was late; therefore we, left.
It was late therefore, we left.

questions.q: Which is punctuated correctly?
Which can join two ICs with only a comma before it?
Which means the same as Although it was cold, we swam?
c: It was cold; for example, we swam.
It was cold; moreover, we swam.
It was cold; therefore, we swam.
It was cold; however, we swam.

questions.q: He didn't revise; ___, he played games all night.
Which is a comma splice?
c: The test was easy; however, I failed.
Although the test was easy, I failed.
The test was easy, but I failed.
The test was easy, however I failed.

questions.q: Cities are noisy. ___, villages are quiet.
